summary: Authored a wasm echo component (binds an aether.tcp listener naming itself as BindListener.consumer, handles SessionData, re-frames the body, writes back via TcpWasmExt::session + SessionWrite) and a raw framed TCP driver that splits frames across writes and reassembles replies with aether_codec::frame::pop_frame. Both crates compiled green (component to wasm32-unknown-unknown, driver native). The end-to-end round-trip FAILED, blocked engine-side: the aether.tcp session delivers each reassembled frame to its bound consumer via ctx.send_to_named(consumer, SessionData), which routes through mailbox_id_from_name — a single-segment hash that (per its own doc) 'yields an id the registry never registered' for a /-rendered lineage path and silently warn-drops the mail (the guarding debug_assert compiles out in the release substrate). A wasm component's own address is always the /-rendered lineage form (aether.component/aether.embedded:NAME), so a component naming itself as consumer can never receive SessionData, and there is no consumer-side workaround. Verified positively that the same component receives SessionData fine over the MCP registry path (a direct send fired on_data), isolating the fault to the socket delivery's flat-hash name resolution. Diagnosis required reading crate internals (tcp/session/runtime.rs, listener/runtime.rs, native/ctx.rs, native/spawn_thread.rs, aether-data/hash.rs) because the whole aether.tcp surface is undocumented in docs/guide. Engine 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003 left alive with the listener bound on 127.0.0.1:7777; it is a headless chassis so there is no capturable frame (this TCP task produces no visual artifact).

artifact.rationale: capture_frame on engine 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003 returned no frame — the substrate is headless/windowless and the recipient settled without a frame reply (MCP -32603: frame capture emits no frame on a windowless substrate). The expected artifact was explicitly "none — transport-only," so there is nothing renderable to judge visually. Substrate terminated to free the fleet.

papercut.where: SessionWrite reply path vs SessionData inbound (framing asymmetry)
papercut.what: Inbound is deframed for you (SessionData.bytes is the reassembled body), but the outbound SessionWrite writes raw bytes with NO framing, so any echo/forward consumer must hand-roll the 4-byte LE length prefix to stay on-wire. aether_codec::frame::encode_frame does not help: it wire-encodes (postcard) the value, so encode_frame(&Vec<u8>) double-encodes (adds a postcard length varint) rather than prepending a raw length prefix. There is no public primitive that just length-prefixes raw bytes.
papercut.suggested: Add aether_codec::frame::prepend_length(&[u8]) -> Vec<u8> (raw 4-byte LE prefix, the inverse of pop_frame), and/or a TcpWasmExt helper like session_write_framed(...) that frames the body — restoring symmetry with the auto-deframed inbound side.

papercut.what: To name itself as consumer a component must hardcode the string "aether.component/aether.embedded:" + NAMESPACE. WasmCtx exposes mailbox_id() (a MailboxId, not usable as a consumer name) but no way to get the component's own registered mailbox NAME. The convention prefix is only discoverable from a recipe. (Compounding the blocker above: the exact self-name a component must construct is precisely the /-path that send_to_named cannot route.)
papercut.suggested: Add ctx.self_name()/self_consumer_name() returning the component's registered lineage address, so a self-registering consumer doesn't guess the aether.component/aether.embedded: convention.

papercut.where: actor_logs MCP tool addressing tcp listener/session mailboxes
papercut.what: actor_logs on the documented listener/session names (aether.tcp.listener:echo, .../aether.tcp.session:conn-0) returns 'mailbox ... not registered on engine' — those lineage-nested actors aren't resolvable by that flat name for logs, and their host-side tracing (tcp session opened/closed, frame-rejected) goes to substrate stderr, not the actor rings. So the tcp transport is effectively unobservable through the MCP harness; I could only diagnose by reading the raw substrate stderr (tunnel.log).
papercut.suggested: Make tcp listener/session actors' log rings reachable by their lineage names via actor_logs, or route their host tracing into a queryable ring, so tcp diagnosis doesn't require host-file access.

papercut.where: spawn_substrate selector for the default headless chassis
papercut.what: spawn_substrate(selector: "default") errors 'no binary in the registry matched selector default'. The tool/guide docs say 'default' is the headless chassis; you must OMIT the selector entirely instead of passing the literal string 'default'.
papercut.suggested: Either accept the literal selector "default" as an alias for the omitted case, or clarify in the tool description that 'default' means omit-the-field (not a passable token).

doc-gap.where: docs/guide (SUMMARY.md has no aether.tcp entry) — the entire BindListener/SessionData/SessionWrite/consumer/framing surface
doc-gap.what: The aether.tcp capability is completely undocumented in the guide: no recipe, no subsystem page, no mention of the inbound wire frame format (4-byte LE length prefix), how consumer delivery works, or that SessionWrite writes raw bytes (no framing). The only reference is ADR-0145, a higher-tier proposal that explicitly leaves the transport 'undesigned' here. To use the surface at all — and to diagnose the silent-drop blocker — I had to read crate internals (session/runtime.rs, listener/runtime.rs, native ctx/spawn_thread send_to_named, aether-data/hash.rs). A real consumer cannot do this.
doc-gap.suggested: Add a docs/guide recipe (mirror serving-http.md) for the aether.tcp transport: the BindListener/consumer model, the SessionData delivery contract, the 4-byte LE length-prefix wire format, that SessionWrite is raw/unframed, and the TcpWasmExt::session reply pattern — with a worked echo example.

blocker.where: BindListener.consumer / aether.tcp session inbound delivery (tcp/session/runtime.rs on_data_ready -> ctx.send_to_named)
blocker.what: A wasm component that names ITSELF as the listener's consumer never receives any SessionData. The session delivers via ctx.send_to_named(consumer, SessionData), which resolves the name with mailbox_id_from_name (a single-segment FNV hash). A loaded component's address is the /-rendered lineage form aether.component/aether.embedded:NAME; hashing that whole string yields an id the registry never registered, so the frame is silently dropped (the /-path debug_assert compiles out in the release substrate). Confirmed by experiment: the same component's on_data fires when SessionData is sent over the MCP registry path, but never via the real socket. There is no guest-side workaround since a component cannot register at a single-segment name.
blocker.suggested: Resolve the consumer name in the tcp session (on_data_ready and the SessionClosed path) through the registry / mailbox_id_from_path (lineage fold) instead of mailbox_id_from_name, so a /-rendered hosted-component consumer routes correctly — the same resolution the MCP Call recipient path already uses. Alternatively, if consumers are intended to be depth-1-root/singleton only (per ADR-0145's native gateway), document that BindListener.consumer must be a single-segment name and reject a /-path early rather than silently dropping.
